results.why: Deck A leaves out Resonating Lute, one of the three requested centerpieces, and runs Tablet of Discovery in its place. Deck B plays all three requested cards. Lute's instant/sorcery mana pairs naturally with its heavy instant suite and ramps into Jeskai Revelation, and it has more interaction (Get Lost, full Helix and No More Lies) to survive until then. Its 26 lands, Great Hall included, cover the black splash for Inevitable Defeat reasonably well.

Deck A plays all three requested cards, including 3 Resonating Lute, which powers out the 7-mana Jeskai Revelation and keeps the hand full for its draw ability. Its control shell of counters, Helix, Get Lost and Day of Judgment hangs together. Deck B leaves out Resonating Lute entirely and swaps in Tablet of Discovery, so it fails the core request despite a reasonable shell.

Deck B actually builds around all three cards. It runs 4 Jolly Balloon Man with real red sources (Spider Manifestation, Stomping Ground, Sacred Foundry, Passage, Gene Pollinator, Bloom Tender) and gives it great copy targets like Formidable Speaker, Ouroboroid and a hasty Craterhoof ETB on a dork-heavy ramp plan. Deck A plays a single Balloon Man with almost no red mana and pads itself with incoherent pieces like 4 Stormchaser's Talent and few spells to support them.

Deck A actually builds around all three requested cards, running 4 Jolly Balloon Man alongside mana creatures. Bloom Tender, Cam untaps and Formidable Speaker feed a big payoff in Craterhoof, Ouroboroid and Gearhulk copies, and the mana supports red and white. Deck B plays a single Balloon Man with Starting Town as its only red source, so a named centerpiece is effectively absent, and its plan of bounce, Otters and Mockingbird is unfocused.

Deck B keeps the Dwarf-equipment core intact and adds seven cheap burn spells, giving it real interaction to clear blockers and answer opposing threats, which Deck A almost entirely lacks. Its equipment suite (Jitte, Spider-Suit, Mattock, Mjölnir) all works with Mauler and Kíli, and its curve and 22 lands are tight. Deck A has strong pieces like Leyline Axe and Thorin, Mountain-king, but it wastes slots on Doc Ock's Tentacles with no 5-drops and runs a clunky 23-land, all-in build.

Deck A pairs the Dwarf-equipment engine with seven cheap removal spells (Burst Lightning, Shock) and strong payoffs like Hard-Won Jitte, Dáin Ironfoot and Mjölnir, so it can both race and interact. Deck B has almost no interaction outside Thorin's ETB trigger and runs dead weight like Doc Ock's Tentacles with no 5-drops to trigger it, plus a clunkier equipment mix. Both mana bases work, but A's plan is tighter and more tournament-ready.

Deck B is a coherent mono-black aristocrats shell with flawless mana. It pairs Umbral Collar Zealot's free sac outlet with endlessly recursive fodder (Bloodghast, Forsaken Miner, Nine-Lives Familiar, Rat King) and doubles up on drain with Popular Egotist alongside the Sackville-Bagginses, while targeted removal and drain triggers routinely commit crimes for the Miner. Deck A has some power in Rottenmouth Viper, but its three-color mana on 21 lands is shaky, especially only ~9 red sources for Biotech Specialist, and its sac fodder is less resilient.

Deck A is a tight mono-black aristocrats shell with clean mana. Recursive fodder (Bloodghast, Forsaken Miner, Nine-Lives Familiar, Rat King) feeds Umbral Collar Zealot as a free sac outlet, while Popular Egotist and The Sackville-Bagginses double up the drain. Deck B stretches into three colors for Biotech Specialist on a shaky red base of shocks, Starting Town and Gene Pollinator, and its loose Lively Dirge and Mutagen Man package makes it less consistent than A's focused plan.

Deck B is a clean Boros superfriends list: 4 Solitary Cell and 4 Gideon's Memorial alongside efficient removal (Burst Lightning, Get Lost, Sear, Helix) and a manabase of all R/W sources. Deck A cuts Solitary Cell to two and spends slots on loose pieces like Way of the Pyromancer, The Mind Stone, Sunken Citadel and Fountainport. Its colorless lands also strain the RR and WW costs, and Day of Judgment fights its own token plan.

Deck A runs the full four Solitary Cell alongside four Memorial and three Ajani Unrelenting. Its plan is coherent: cheap removal and Cell protect a dense planeswalker suite, Voice of Victory makes tokens for Memorial to pump, and 17 legendaries keep Cell's draw ability live. Deck B trims Cell to two, plays clunky one-ofs like The Mind Stone and Aang's Iceberg, and strains its mana with three colorless Fountainports and tapped Citadels, making it a less focused and less consistent shell.

Deck B is a tighter stompy shell: Ouroboroid and Trudge reach 7 power quickly for Fight Rigging, while Kiora and Outcaster Trailblazer turn big bodies into card advantage alongside Henge. Deck A spends slots on clunky toolbox targets like Emrakul (poor in mono-green), Bahamut and Titan, and its Nykthos package has little devotion to support it. That makes A's plan slower and less coherent.

Deck A uses the proven Pioneer mono-green engine pieces. Ouroboroid quickly turns on Fight Rigging's power-7 clause and makes Slumbering Trudge huge. Kiora and Outcaster Trailblazer keep the cards flowing and can untap Nykthos or the Henge, and Life's Legacy cashes in a big Trudge. Deck B leans on clunky top-end like Emrakul (which barely gets discounted in a mono-green graveyard) and Summon: Bahamut, with no Ouroboroid-style accelerant, so its plan is slower and less consistent.

Deck B is a coherent mono-white heroic shell with 18 creatures, including the heroic payoffs Phalanx Leader and Hero of Iroas. It runs a full suite of cheap targeting spells and protection (Gods Willing, Feat, Sejiri Shelter), and its mana is clean. Deck A runs only 14 creatures against 26 pump spells, leans on filler like Academic Dispute and an off-plan Speedball, and makes the three requested cards a smaller part of a scattered Boros pile.

Deck A is a coherent mono-white heroic shell that fits the requested cards: Phalanx Leader, Homestead Courage and Dual-Sun Technique reward the +1/+1 counter theme. It also carries real protection in Gods Willing, Feat of Resistance and Sejiri Shelter, and its mana is nearly flawless. Deck B is a red-leaning prowess deck with a clunky three-mana Practiced Offense, and filler like Academic Dispute and Speedball that dilutes the plan built around the requested cards.

Deck B is a more complete Jeskai control shell. No More Lies, Supreme Verdict, Get Lost, Sear and The Wandering Emperor cover combo, creatures and planeswalkers while the deck works toward resolving 7-mana Revelations. Deck A has no counterspells, and its Fiery Impulse, Erode and Farewell package leaves it weak to combo and noncreature threats, a serious hole for a Pioneer deck built on expensive instants. Both mana bases have about nine black sources for Inevitable Defeat, so B's broader interaction decides it.

Both decks are legal 60-card shells with Tablet, Defeat and Revelation and similar black-source counts. Deck A rounds out the control plan better, with No More Lies for interaction against combo and big spells, efficient removal in Sear and Get Lost, a cheaper sweeper in Supreme Verdict, and The Wandering Emperor as a flexible finisher. Deck B has no counterspells and leans on Fiery Impulse and six-mana Farewell, which leaves it weaker against the field.

Deck B pairs the threats with efficient cheap instants: Fiery Impulse, Burst Lightning, Lightning Axe, Opt and Sleight of Hand fuel delve-style cost reduction while answering creatures, which is the proven shape of Terror decks. Deck A's interaction is almost entirely bounce plus Bushwhack fights, and filler like Stormchaser's Talent and Cache Grab leaves it soft to aggro. B's three-color mana stretches for a green splash, but 8 green sources for one-mana Bushwhacks is workable.

Deck A is a tight Temur tempo shell. It has 33 cheap instants and sorceries to shrink Terror and Crab, real interaction (Fiery Impulse, Burst Lightning, Lightning Axe, Spell Pierce), and a clean green splash for Bushwhack. Deck B's Beanstalk and self-bounce engine is cute, but its interaction is almost entirely bounce and fight, so it struggles against opposing threats and fast decks.

Deck B is not Modern-legal because it runs four Faithless Looting, which is banned in the format. That disqualifies it outright, and its 42 spells on 18 lands with off-color Phoenix bestow is also shaky. Deck A is a legal, coherent mono-black graveyard deck: Supplier, Overlord and Street Wraith fill the yard, Persist and Emperor bring back Archon, Flare uses the cheap creatures as free sacrifice fodder, and the mana is solid.

Deck A pairs Persist with Faithless Looting, Eyetwitch and Stitcher's Supplier, so it can reliably bin Archon of Cruelty on turn two and reanimate it. Bloodghast and Village Rites supply sac fodder and card flow around Flare of Malice, and the interaction is real. Deck B mostly relies on random mills to find Archon, has few true discard outlets, and runs four tapped Crypts plus four colorless Towers, making it slower and less consistent.

Deck A leaves out Turntimber Symbiosis entirely, one of the three cards the request named, so it fails the brief. It is a polished Eldrazi ramp list, but not the requested deck. Deck B plays all three named cards as full playsets inside a coherent Eldrazi/Fight Rigging ramp shell, with a real mana base (Sprawl, Halfling, Talismans, Temples, Labyrinths) and Turntimber doubling as a land that can pull a pumped Trudge or a fatty toward the Rigging threshold.

Deck B omits Turntimber Symbiosis entirely, so it fails the core request. Deck A plays all three named cards as four-ofs inside a coherent Eldrazi-ramp shell. Halfling, Utopia Sprawl and Talisman feed Trudge's X, Fight Rigging's 7-power threshold, and Temple/Labyrinth-powered Emrakul and Sire, on a reasonable 19 lands plus 4 MDFCs.

Deck B is a coherent UB storm shell. Dark Ritual, LED, Infernal Tutor and Paradoxical Outcome fuel the Riddlesmith and Echo of Eons loops, and Tendrils is a real, tutorable kill. Its blue-black fetch/dual manabase actually casts Ovalchase Daredevil, rituals and Echo. Deck A has almost no black sources for Daredevil, a thin and awkward land base, and a single untutorable-in-practice Grapeshot, so its plan is far less reliable.

Deck A runs Vault of Whispers and Seat of the Synod, which are banned in Legacy, so it isn't tournament-legal as written. Deck B is a legal 60. It has a coherent artifact-chaining shell: Baubles and Petals feed Riddlesmith, Does Machines and Urza's Saga, while Echo of Eons and Gamble lead into Grapeshot. Its black mana for Daredevil is thin, but it can still be registered and played.

Deck B is a coherent Phoenix chain deck. Faithless Looting and Buried Alive bin the birds, and free or cheap spells like Mutagenic Growth, Gut Shot, Lava Dart (with flashback) and Ritual make three-spell turns easy, while burn adds reach. Deck A spends slots on Daze, Thoughtseize and a Fantasticar subtheme, leaving fewer free triggers and a thinner red base for its namesake engine.

Deck A gives Buried Alive a real way to return the Phoenixes the same turn. Dark Ritual into Buried Alive plus free or cheap spells like Gut Shot, Mutagenic Growth and Lava Dart (with flashback) reaches three instants and sorceries, and Faithless Looting and Flow State add more velocity and spell count. Deck B dilutes the plan with four The Fantasticar, an off-theme three-mana artifact, and has fewer cheap ways to reach the spell count, so its Phoenix engine is clunkier.

Deck A is a coherent mono-white go-wide shell: free bodies (Ornithopter, Phyrexian Walker) power out Search Party Captain, Salt Road Packbeast and Leonardo, while also turning on Springleaf Drum and Ramosian Rally. Its artifact count supports Ardent Recruit, and 14 lands are fine at this curve. Deck B is a reasonable Boros artifact deck with good removal, but it dilutes the requested core with bounce creatures and burn, and has a clunkier two-color, tapped-land manabase.

Deck A is a coherent Boros artifact aggro shell. Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher rebuy Springleaf Drum and the Clues, artifact lands turn on Ardent Recruit and metalcraft Galvanic Blast, and Bolt, Journey and Thraben Charm give it real interaction. Deck B is a pile of go-wide filler like Phyrexian Walker and Ornithopter with no removal. It leans on its Ramosian Rallies, so it folds to any sweeper or blocker-heavy board.

Deck B is a coherent Boros midrange shell where the Eidolons and Spirit Mascot really matter. It runs 18 multicolored spells to rebuy the Eidolons, and disturb plus flashback leave the graveyard to grow Mascot. It also has real interaction in Bolt and Journey and a clean two-color manabase. Deck A splices a fringe Tireless Tribe/Inside Out combo onto the request with one Fling, and its four Sneaky Snackers are UB cards that only work as discard fodder, so the requested cards end up peripheral to a fragile plan.

Deck A is a coherent Boros midrange shell where Mascot and both Eidolons get real support. Plenty of multicolored spells (Halberdiers, Skyknight, Recruit, Thrilling Discovery, Pursue, Martial Glory) rebuy the Eidolons, while flashback, disturb and Eidolon recursion grow Mascot, all on a clean 18-land R/W manabase. Deck B splices together unrelated packages (the Tireless Tribe/Inside Out/Fling combo, Sneaky Snacker discard-draw), so the requested cards are only side pieces in a deck pulling in several directions.

Deck B uses all three requested cards well: Survival, Pattern, Bombardment, Cabal Therapy and Phyrexian Tower turn Veteran Explorer and Academy Rector deaths into value. Three Future Sights plus Wall of Blossoms keep the engine refilling, and Deranged Hermit and Bombardment give it real ways to win. Deck A runs only one Future Sight, wastes slots on three Gaea's Blessing, and relies on Decree of Silence and three Krosan Tuskers with almost no real kill, so it does less of what was asked.

Deck A is a coherent Survival/Rector toolbox. Rector fetches Future Sight or Survival, Explorer ramps into the UUU, and Bombardment, Hermit, Wurm and Karmic Guide give it real sacrifice outlets and kill conditions. Deck B is closer to the old Rector/Decree control shell, but it runs only one Future Sight. It also has very few creatures to sacrifice and almost no way to win beyond three Krosan Tuskers, and Gaea's Blessing is filler.

Deck B actually builds around the requested cards: four Colossus, four Rhystic Tutor and four Utopia Tree in a fast, coherent Buried Alive/Survival reanimator shell. Putrid Imp and Survival act as discard outlets, Dark Ritual and Petal add speed, and the mana supports B/R/G. Deck A treats Colossus and Rhystic Tutor as afterthoughts and splashes Nicol Bolas (UU) with almost no blue sources, so it reads as a loose Sneak/Survival pile rather than the requested brew.

Deck A is a focused, fast reanimator shell. Buried Alive, Putrid Imp, Survival and four Rhystic Tutors put Colossus in the graveyard, and Exhume, Reanimate, Animate Dead and Dark Ritual bring it back early, giving consistent redundancy on a sound 16-land-plus-Petal mana base. Deck B is a clunky Sneak Attack pile with 22 lands plus 8 dorks, scattered oddball threats like Genesis and Nishoba, and too little card flow and tutoring to assemble its combo reliably.
